hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation (gate self-test on this piece's surface)
hard_gates.evidence: No real leak found in the product: my own probes as Al Noor against Gulf Steel through the palette's sources, user and company ids, PUT /me/preferences carrying B's ids in the body plus X-Tenant headers in all four language/digits combinations, tenant query parameters and the CSV print found 0 of 18 B markers, and B's preferences did not change (isolation-probe.txt). All 17 tenant tables have RLS enabled and forced. erp_app is not superuser, cannot bypass RLS and sees 0 users with no tenant set. Three of the four plants I put in p04's surface were caught. L1 (a static memo of the previous Arabic caller, sent in a response header) was caught by G1ProcessStateTests and by G1HttpIsolationTests (11 leaks, both directions, Arabic sessions). C2 (palette answers memoised on the extension registry) was caught by clientIsolation.test.tsx. The r4 Arabic-path gap stays fixed. MISSED: plant L3 (plant-server-L3-count-header.diff). PUT /api/identity/me/preferences keeps a process-wide count of Arabic switches across all tenants on IConfiguration, a framework singleton, and returns it only in the response header X-Arabic-Switches. All 60 G1 tests passed with it in place (plants-serverL3-gates.log): G1ProcessState, G1HttpIsolation (36 min) and G1NonInterference (15 min). The leak is real: on the planted build, tenant A's count went from 2 to 8 while tenant B switched five times (plant-L3-live-demo.txt).

Plant P1 was caught by 2 G2PermissionTests (anonymous endpoint missing from the allowlist, reviewed prefix) (plants-serverA-gates.log). P1 added an anonymous POST /api/identity/me/preferences/reset that resets the caller's language with no permission check. Plant P2 was caught by AppShell.test.tsx ('preferences without the permission to change the profile'). P2 saved language changes to the server without the identity.profile.update check. In the browser the viewer's palette offers no New user, New role or New company ('Nothing matches'), and Alt+N on Users does nothing for them. The no-access user sees only shell actions. The verify's palette, identity, tenancy and keyboard plant self-tests reported 10, 13, 24 and 18 plants, all caught.

biggest_gap.title: A cross-tenant leak with no marker on the shell's own preferences endpoint passes every G1 gate, because the non-interference check never compares response headers
biggest_gap.detail: G1NonInterference is the check meant to catch leaks that carry nothing recognisable of tenant B's: a count, an order, a timing. It compares only the status code and the body of each answer (NonInterference.GetAsync returns '<status> <normalised body>', and the write comparisons are built the same way). The marker-based HTTP attack judges headers, but only for B's ids, e-mails, codes and canaries. G1ProcessState inspects static fields and walks product singletons, but not values written into framework singletons such as IConfiguration. So a process-wide count, sent back in a response header and stored outside a static field, is invisible to all three. I planted exactly that on PUT /api/identity/me/preferences, the shell's own endpoint and its Arabic path: it returns how many Arabic switches the whole process has seen, across tenants. All 60 G1 tests passed, and on the running build tenant A can watch tenant B's activity. This is the kind of leak real code produces, such as rate-limit headers, an ETag or version counter, or X-Total-Count kept in a shared cache. Every later module (invoices, stock, journals) will add headers and caches, and they inherit the same blind spot. The fix lies in the shared G1 machinery (owned with p00), but it fails this round because the fault is on p04's surface. Fix: (1) In NonInterference, compare normalised response headers for GETs and writes, dropping Date, trace and request ids and normalising Set-Cookie values, and add a ratchet count of compared headers. (2) In G1ProcessState, snapshot the in-memory values of IConfiguration and the other framework singletons before and after both tenants' activity, or make runtime writes to IConfiguration fail. (3) Add this plant to the self-noninterference self-tests so it stays caught.
biggest_gap.evidence: In a clone at 8bc6a09, apply gauntlet/evidence/p04-shell/r8/plant-server-L3-count-header.diff (ProfileEndpoints.UpdatePreferences: on language=ar or numerals=arab, increment IConfiguration['Erp:ArabicSwitches'] and return it in the header X-Arabic-Switches). Run dotnet test tests/Erp.Gates.Tests with filter 'FullyQualifiedName~Erp.Gates.Tests.G1&Load!=Timing&Process!=self-http&Process!=self-company&Process!=self-noninterference'. Result: 60 of 60 passed, including G1HttpIsolationTests (36 m) and G1NonInterferenceTests (15 m) (plants-serverL3-gates.log). Live check with ./erp up on the planted build and drivers/plant-L3-live.mjs: admin@alnoor.example switches to Arabic twice (counts 1 and 2), admin@gulfsteel.example switches five times (3 to 7), and Al Noor's next switch reads X-Arabic-Switches: 8 (plant-L3-live-demo.txt). For contrast, the same leak carrying B's e-mail (plant L1) is caught by both G1HttpIsolation and G1ProcessState (plants-serverA-gates.log).
